labels.label: (no ETT label; layer 1) Causal.Causality.ChronalPastNeighbours.hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere / ChronalFutureNeighbours.hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere, with the point forms .hasChronalNeighbour
labels.notes: These are the lemmas the target title names (ladder.toml:2538). The hypothesis is h : C.ChronalPastNeighbours (resp. ChronalFutureNeighbours), with [TopologicalSpace M] only, and the conclusion is the ladder's node: [[property]] has_chronal_neighbour has lean = "Causal.Causality.HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere" (ladder.toml:752-754), defined as forall p, C.HasChronalNeighbour p (ChronalNeighbourBridge.lean:107), where HasChronalNeighbour p is (C.Iplus top {p}).Nonempty or (C.Iminus top {p}).Nonempty (LocateExtension.lean:138). The past form gives the Or.inr side and the future form the Or.inl side, as the docstrings say. The module docstring has no **`label`** mark, which is correct because no label is certified.

labels.label: Causal.notchedCausality_separates_hasChronalNeighbour (the notched plane with the node)
labels.notes: Compared conjunct by conjunct with Causal.notchedCausality_separates (NotchedPlane.lean:798-812; 20 conjuncts). All 20 are present in their original relative order, plus 4 more: HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere (the ladder's node, in its own name), forall W : Opens notchedPlane, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W (notchedCausality_absolutelyMinimalOn), ChronalPastNeighbours and not ChronalFutureNeighbours. Every id of the `from` of ladder.toml:2545 is a conjunct, and not Tarentin is the last one. The extra conjuncts are kernel-checked and described accurately. AbsolutelyMinimalOn W is the every-cover, every-sub-open condition (Generated.lean:239), so 'either reading' of DEC-167 holds whichever way OQ-95 is answered: the hereditary form is the stronger one. not ChronalFutureNeighbours is derived from ChronalPastNeighbours together with not ChronalNeighbours.

labels.label: Causal.notchedCausality_dual_separates_hasChronalNeighbour (the time-reversed plane, through the future form)
labels.notes: Compared with Causal.notchedCausality_dual_separates (NotchedPlane.lean:832-843; 20 conjuncts). All 20 are present in order, plus dual.HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere (through ChronalFutureNeighbours.hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere and dual_chronalFutureNeighbours), forall W, dual.AbsolutelyMinimalOn W, dual.ChronalFutureNeighbours and not dual.ChronalPastNeighbours. Every id of the `from` of ladder.toml:2397 is carried, has_chronal_neighbour as well, and not LocallyCausallyOpenFuture is present.

labels.label: Causal.globalLine_separates_hasChronalNeighbour (the global line with the node)
labels.notes: Compared with Causal.globalLine_separates (ChronalNeighbourBridge.lean:472-475; 7 conjuncts). All 7 are present in order, after HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere and Tarentin (Causal.globalLine_tarentin, ChronalTarentin.lean:208). It therefore also carries all 6 conjuncts of Causal.globalLine_separates_tarentin (ChronalTarentin.lean:224). The `from` and `to` of ladder.toml:1910, 1884 and 1891 are covered. 'No causality with gluing' is stated both as the conjunct not AbsolutelyMinimal and in the docstrings (file lines 47-49 and 227-228), consistent with DEC-167 (registers/DECISIONS.md:178).

labels.label: Bare forms not_tarentin_of_hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere_bare / not_absolutelyMinimal_of_hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere_bare
labels.notes: Neither is vacuous: each is a not-forall over M : Type with [T2Space] and [SecondCountableTopology], refuted by a concrete witness that meets every hypothesis (the notched plane, resp. the global line). The first quantifies over the class 'forall W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W' and its docstring says it holds in either reading, which is true because the witness is hereditarily absolutely minimal. This follows the precedent not_locallyCausallyOpen_of_causallyPlain_bare. The second's docstring (lines 257-258) says it holds in the no-gluing reading only, and REPORT.json says the declaration goes away with the DEC-167 refactor, which is correct: under gluing the refuted implication becomes true. One wording problem in the first docstring: see finding 1.

findings.what: The docstring of not_tarentin_of_hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere_bare says 'the notched plane, whose chronal neighbours are all to the past'. Read literally, this is false. Points off the notch's edge have chronal futures: notchedChronalStep (NotchedPlane.lean:133) is a strict increase in both null coordinates along a segment in U, so for example (-1,-1) is chronologically before (-1/2,-1/2). What holds is ChronalPastNeighbours together with not ChronalFutureNeighbours: the edge points (0 <= u and 0 <= v, notchedCausality_not_lt_of_mem_edge) have no chronal future. ('No chronal future neighbours' at lines 39-40 and 136 is the property's name, as in the library's 'no chronal neighbours', and is fine.)
findings.fix: Write '... the notched plane, which has chronal past neighbours in every open set but not chronal future neighbours (the points of the notch's edge have no chronal future)'.

findings.what: The REPORT says ChronalFutureNeighbours becoming a node is something 'which DEC-166 (a) and the ladder's comment at 703-735 decline'. DEC-166 (a) (registers/DECISIONS.md:177) only moves the one-sided notions to the future base. The ladder says 'No node of one fixed side is added (the keeper's call; not ruled)' (programme/ladder.toml:312). The '(no node)' remark in the has_chronal_neighbour comment is at ladder.toml:737, outside 703-735. The question is open for the keeper, not ruled against.
findings.fix: Write 'which the keeper has not added (ladder.toml:312, "the keeper's call; not ruled"; :737)', and drop the attribution to DEC-166 (a).

findings.what: The simulation adds tarentin to the `from` of ladder.toml:1910, but the 1910 proposal does not propose it: it only re-points the entry. The effect is harmless. A superset of `from` ids with the same witness can only add has-properties, so the clean result also covers the proposal as written, and the witness does carry Tarentin. Still, the keeper reads two different proposals.
findings.fix: In lemmas_for_the_keeper[1], add 'optionally, tarentin can join `from` (the witness carries it; simulated: no pair moves)', or describe the simulation as covering the proposal plus that optional id.
